 ATP Finals 2026: How much Zverev, Alcaraz, Shelton and Medvedev have already made
 Originally posted on
 TennisUpToDate.com 
  | 
 Last updated Nov 21, 2026 12:50 AM ET
 Add us as a preferred source on Google
 The four semi-finalists at the ATP Finals have already secured more than $1 million in prize money, but there is still a significant amount up for grabs as the tournament reaches its decisive stage in Turin. Alexander Zverev , Carlos Alcaraz , Ben Shelton and Daniil Medvedev have all booked their places in the last four, with the eventual champion potentially taking home more than $5 million. 
 This year's tournament features a record total prize pool of $15.75 million, making it one of the most lucrative events on the tennis calendar. The singles champion can earn up to $5,171,000, provided he wins all five of his matches during the week without suffering a defeat. 
 However, not every semi-finalist enters the knockout rounds with the same amount already guaranteed. Zverev and Alcaraz completed the group stage unbeaten, collecting three victories apiece, while Shelton and Medvedev each finished with a 2-1 record. 
 That difference means the German and Spaniard have earned $405,000 more than their semi-final opponents before Saturday's matches. Nevertheless, all four players have the same additional prize money available through the semi-finals and final, meaning there is still plenty to play for beyond the trophy itself. 
 How much have Zverev, Alcaraz, Shelton and Medvedev earned?
 The ATP Finals prize money system is divided into several stages. Every singles player receives a participation fee, which is worth $338,000 for completing all three round-robin matches. Players also receive $405,000 for every victory during the group stage, regardless of whether they finish first or second in their group. 
 The semi-finals and final offer considerably larger rewards, with $1,206,000 available for winning a semi-final and another $2,412,000 for winning the championship match. 
 Based on those figures, the four remaining players have already secured the following amounts:

 Zverev and Alcaraz are therefore level financially after completing perfect group campaigns. The German defeated Rafael Jodar, Shelton and Arthur Fils, while Alcaraz overcame Frances Tiafoe, Medvedev and Flavio Cobolli without dropping a set. 
 Shelton and Medvedev have earned the same amount despite competing in different groups. The American recovered from his opening defeat against Zverev by beating Fils and Jodar, while Medvedev secured victories against Cobolli and Tiafoe after losing to Alcaraz. 
 The participation fee is an important part of the calculation. It is not automatically paid in full to every player at the start of the tournament: it is adjusted according to the number of round-robin matches completed. In this case, all four semi-finalists played their three scheduled matches, so each has received the full $338,000. 
 How much more can they win at the ATP Finals?
 The next step offers an additional $1,206,000 to each player who wins his semi-final. Reaching the championship match therefore guarantees Zverev and Alcaraz a total of $2,759,000, while Shelton and Medvedev would increase their earnings to $2,354,000. 
 There is no additional payment for losing the final. Instead, the winner receives another $2,412,000, taking his total earnings to either $5,171,000 or $4,766,000, depending on his group-stage record.

 Zverev will face Medvedev in the second semi-final, while Alcaraz takes on Shelton in the opening match. Both former champions have already secured substantial earnings, but Zverev and Medvedev will also be competing for a place in the final with the chance to claim another major payday. 
 For Alcaraz, the tournament represents an opportunity to win his first ATP Finals title after finishing runner-up last year. Shelton, meanwhile, has reached the semi-finals for the first time and is now just two victories away from the biggest title of his career. 
 Ultimately, the financial difference between the four players comes down to their group-stage results. However, the remaining $3,618,000 available to each semi-finalist means that the biggest rewards are still within reach, with the champion set to leave Turin with at least $4.766 million.
